brief.text:
GANGSTAS PARADISE (Sleeper) — FINAL WEEK 1: lost 118.06-151.56 to AdufortheWin84, now 0-1 — you started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs (15.5) sitting on your own bench, a 9.8-point unforced error; Zay Flowers' huge day (26.0, 150 yds, 1 TD) ended with a re-aggravated hamstring, and Schefter now calls a Week 2 return "unrealistic"
Do now: bench Zay Flowers, start Stefon Diggs in his place — Diggs draws Dallas, which allowed the most passing yards in the league last year, a legitimate smash-spot consolation prize. Official practice status doesn't post until Wednesday, so recheck, but plan on Diggs.
Locks next 24h: none — nothing on your roster plays until Sunday 1pm ET, and no rostered player is in Thursday's DET@BUF opener
Lineup: Diggs in for Flowers is the only change. Chase Brown and Higgins draw Houston, the consensus #1 defense in football — expect a grind on volume, not a shootout. Strange and Tuten both travel to Denver, a tough matchup on paper (Broncos allowed the 3rd-fewest yards per carry to RBs last year) but there's no better option on your bench for either. Aubrey is a smash play at home vs Washington, 27.0 implied team total. If Flowers somehow gets cleared Wednesday, this call reverses.
Waivers / trades: see the Waivers tab — Samaje Perine and Mike Gesicki are this week's top two adds; see the Trades tab for a Tyler Shough-for-Kaelon Black offer going out to Emeka Eggbucock

GAME OF THROWS (Yahoo) — no fresh screenshot for a third straight run — Week 1 final score is STILL unconfirmed and I'm flying blind on your Week 2 lineup, working off preseason projections and public schedules only — SEND A SCREENSHOT
Do now: drop a Week 1 final box score AND a current Week 2 matchup screenshot into the War room Drive folder. The newest file in there is still the same pre-kickoff Week 1 image from three runs ago — I can't confirm your actual roster, your Week 1 result, or build real Week 2 projections without it.
Locks next 24h: none
Lineup (best-effort, unconfirmed roster): assuming nothing's changed — Pickens is a smash play at home vs Washington (the league's worst pass defense last year, 27.0 implied), Garrett Wilson gets a plus matchup vs a Packers defense playing without Micah Parsons for roughly six weeks, Stafford is a bounce-back streaming spot at home vs a Giants run defense that just lost Dexter Lawrence in a trade. Isaiah Likely — correction from prior runs, he signed with the Giants as a free agent, not still on Baltimore — draws a brutal Rams defense on Monday night but keeps his role regardless. Judkins is the soft spot: lowest implied team total on the roster (16.0) as a big underdog on the road at Tampa Bay.

waivers.text:
SLEEPER — TE is still priority one (you roster zero backup behind Strange, who shares Week 7's JAX/LAC bye cluster with Herbert, Hampton, and your DEF), but Chase Brown insurance jumped the line since he starts in BOTH your leagues. FAAB budget is untouched at $100, you sit waiver position 3.
1. Samaje Perine (RB, CIN) — confirmed direct backup to Chase Brown, who anchors your RB1 slot in both leagues. Bye-week and injury insurance you currently have nowhere on either roster. Drop Zachariah Branch (WR, no role in ATL). FAAB $14.
2. Mike Gesicki (TE, CIN) — CIN's starting TE (depth chart #1), the single best TE add on the wire and it directly solves your zero-depth problem. Cincinnati's bye is Week 6, a different week than Strange's Week 7 — real coverage, not a redundant bye. Drop Zavion Thomas (WR, no role in CHI). FAAB $16.
3. Kimani Vidal (RB, LAC) — direct committee-mate to your own Omarion Hampton; Chargers' staff has said either back "can be entrusted with the ball." Cheap insurance on a player who's already your RB1. Drop Michael Wilson (WR, buried behind Marvin Harrison Jr./Trey McBride in ARI's target mix). FAAB $8.
4. Evan Engram (TE, DEN) — second starting-caliber TE if you miss on Gesicki, or a pair if you want true bye-week coverage (Denver's bye is Week 10 — different from both Strange's Week 7 and Gesicki's Week 6). Drop Woody Marks (RB, buried in a Houston committee). FAAB $6.
5. Cole Kmet (TE, CHI) — speculative third TE, only worth a bid if you whiff on both Gesicki and Engram; would require cutting whichever of the above you value least once your bench fills. No fixed drop assigned — conditional pickup only.

trades.text:
SLEEPER — send Tyler Shough (New Orleans' actual Week 1 starting QB, currently buried as your QB2 behind Herbert) to Emeka Eggbucock ("Emeka Eggbucock") for Kaelon Black (RB, SF). Their starter Kyler Murray is in the concussion protocol — Carson Wentz starts Week 2 vs Chicago, with Murray's return more likely Week 3 — and they're carrying zero backup QB, so a hot streaming starter has real short-term value to them. They're deep at RB (Ashton Jeanty, Tony Pollard, Javonte Williams, and Black all rostered), so Black is a fair piece to deal from that surplus. For you, Black is a legitimate stash: he out-touched Christian McCaffrey in the second half of Week 1 (15 total touches, tied for the team lead) and Draft Sharks already has him "pulling away" in San Francisco's RB2 race — real insurance and potential standalone value behind a back the 49ers want to manage carefully after a 450-touch 2025. This directly fixes your thinnest bench spot (Woody Marks, a committee back in Houston, is your only other RB depth) without touching Stefon Diggs, who you need starting this week for the injured Zay Flowers. Checked Weeks 15-17 first: moving a buried backup QB for a real RB stash only helps your playoff bench, it doesn't cost you anything there.
